title: How to Calculate Primary Teacher Salary VIC from an Hourly Rate
description: Learn how to convert an hourly rate to annual pay for a primary teacher salary VIC. Includes tax, super, and the 38-hour week assumption. Use our timesheet.
salarySummary: For a primary teacher in Victoria, an hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks gives an annual gross figure, before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary for a primary teacher role in Victoria?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $40 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $79,040 per year. This assumes consistent hours, no unpaid overtime, and no penalty rates. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to check.

faqs.q: What tax will I pay on a primary teacher salary in Victoria?
faqs.a: For the 2026–27 year, resident tax rates apply: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. You also pay a 2% Medicare levy (based on 2025–26 single thresholds). Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for an estimate.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the annual salary figure?
faqs.a: No. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base). Your annual salary figure is gross pay before super. For example, if your annual salary is $80,000, your employer adds $9,600 in super. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly to Annual for Primary Teacher Salary VIC

If you’re looking at a **primary teacher salary VIC** and you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, the first step is understanding how to convert between the two. The standard formula is:

**Annual gross pay ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This article assumes a 38-hour week, which is the typical full-time hours used by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Bureau of Statistics. If your role is part-time or casual, adjust the hours accordingly. For a fortnightly figure, simply multiply the weekly amount by 2.

### Using the Victorian Average as a Reference

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings in Victoria averaged $2,041.10 per week. That is an average across all occupations and industries, not the median for a primary teacher. It can still give you a rough benchmark: if a primary teacher in Victoria earned that weekly amount, their annual gross would be about $106,137 (before tax and super). But remember, this is an average, not a job-specific median. Award rates for teachers under the Victorian Government Schools Agreement or the Independent Schools Award may set different minimums. Always check your specific award or enterprise agreement.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. Most primary teachers are covered by an award or agreement that pays above the minimum. If you are comparing a salary offer, ensure it meets the applicable award rate. The Fair Work Commission sets these rates, and you can find them in [pay guides](/blog).

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you work as a casual primary teacher, your hourly rate typically includes a 25% casual loading. When using our [timesheet](/), do not type a rate that already includes loading; instead, enter the base rate and check the casual loading box. Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (the super guarantee rate for 2026–27). The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. Super is not part of your salary; it is an additional contribution your employer makes.

### Tax and Medicare on Your Annual Figure

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate your take-home pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

You also pay a Medicare levy of 2% (based on the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here). This is an estimate; it does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For a more detailed breakdown, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

### Example Calculation for a Primary Teacher in Victoria

Suppose you are offered an hourly rate of $45 as a full-time primary teacher in Victoria. Assuming 38 hours per week:

- Weekly: $45 × 38 = $1,710
- Fortnightly: $1,710 × 2 = $3,420
- Annual gross: $1,710 × 52 = $88,920

Super (12% on top): $88,920 × 0.12 = $10,670.40 (up to the contribution base)

Tax estimate (using 2026–27 rates and 2% Medicare):
- Tax on $88,920: $5,092 (first $45,000) + 30% on $43,920 = $13,176, total $18,268
- Medicare: $88,920 × 2% = $1,778.40
- Total tax and Medicare: $20,046.40
- Estimated take-home: $88,920 – $20,046.40 = $68,873.60 per year

This is a simplified estimate. Your actual pay may vary due to allowances, penalty rates, or salary sacrifice.

### Important Notes

- The formula assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base.
- Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here.
- HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.
- This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For a quick conversion, use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool or the [timesheet](/) to see your annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures with tax and super estimates. If you are comparing a **primary teacher salary VIC** offer, remember to check the applicable award and include super as an additional benefit.
